name: canvas-design
description: Create beautiful visual art in .png and .pdf documents using design philosophy. You should use this skill when the user asks to create a poster, piece of art, design, or other static piece. Create original visual designs, never copying existing artists' work to avoid copyright violations.

notes: trigger 5: what+when front-loaded ('Create beautiful visual art in .png and .pdf documents... when the user asks to create a poster, piece of art, design, or other static piece') plus a negative-constraint boundary: 'never copying existing artists' work to avoid copyright violations'.

structure 4 (override down from lint 5): otherwise clean 129-line two-step layout, but it embeds a fabricated user turn — 'The user ALREADY said "It isn't perfect enough. It must be pristine, a masterpiece if craftsmanship"' — a manufactured-dialogue anti-pattern, and buries the './canvas-fonts' directory dependency mid-paragraph.

actionability 4 (agree with lint): numbered two-step workflow, explicit anti-patterns ('avoid adding more graphics; instead refine what has been created'), and a forced second-pass verify loop ('Take a second pass. Go back to the code and refine/polish further'), but 0 code examples, no error handling, and no handling for a missing fonts dir ('Search the `./canvas-fonts` directory' assumes it exists).
safety 5: no dangerous patterns; one mild undeclared network instruction — 'Download and use whatever fonts are needed' — with unspecified sources, mitigated by the bundled-fonts-first policy.
portability 5: relative paths only ('./canvas-fonts'), platform-neutral outputs (.md/.pdf/.png), standard frontmatter.
